title: Seva, reviewed
tomorrow: a college tour, three states from home. who'd help her remember?

lines: BEBE: THE SHOES, AT THE GURDWARA.
cards: Simran's calendar looks like a game of Tetris losing badly. Creek on Saturdays, food bank on Tuesdays, tutoring on Thursdays, and a chemistry grade sliding. At dinner Harjit says, pick one and keep it.
Bebe, passing the dal, says, then pick the shoes. Joray seva, at the gurdwara, Sunday mornings, where you started. Harjit says the world needs her more than the shoe rack does.
Bebe raises one eyebrow. Two people Simran loves, two answers.

teach.h: ANG 26: SEVA IN THE MIDST OF THE WORLD.
teach.b: Both views live inside Sikhi, so let each speak. Harjit's case first.

teach.h: THE WORLD IS WHERE THE NEED IS.
teach.b: On Ang 26 Guru Nanak says, in paraphrase: in the midst of this world, do seva, and you'll be given a seat in the Lord's court. In the world. Not after it, not apart from it.
The food bank is the world. The creek is the world. If seva stays behind the gurdwara doors, the hungry on Tuesday wait.

teach.h: THE GURDWARA IS WHERE SEVA IS LEARNED.
teach.b: The gurdwara is where seva is learned. Wiping the shoes of strangers who'll never know your name, in the Guru's presence, with the sangat beside you, scrubs at haumai, the I, I, I, in a way a volunteer badge might not.
And the sangat runs on it: no hands, no langar. Seva in the Guru's house is training for seva everywhere else. Each is a real view Sikhs hold, and some hold both.
Simran hears them out, then tries a month of two: the food bank with Maya on Tuesdays, and the shoe rack with Bebe on Sundays. Tutoring and the creek go to friends who've got more room.
My seva doesn't have to be everything. It has to be kept.

how: Sikhs do seva in the gurdwara, in the langar, cleaning, and joray seva at the shoe rack, and out in the world at food banks, hospitals and relief work; some keep one regular seva in their week.

o: a vow to volunteer for a set number of hours
selfless service, done for others with no wage
a donation made to the gurdwara each month

games.q: two views of seva — tap the pairs.
p: seva in the midst of the world
caring for shoes at the gurdwara
the I, I, I that seva scrubs at
the food bank and the shoe rack

s: Sikhi says seva only counts inside the gurdwara
Guru Nanak on Ang 26: do seva in the midst of the world.
seva in the gurdwara is seen as training against haumai
wiping strangers' shoes in the Guru's presence scrubs at the I, I, I.
the more sevas you keep, the better the seva
Simran drops two so she can keep two. a seva has to be kept.

games.q: Simran leans toward her dad's view. what's the strongest case she could make for Bebe's side?
o: the gurdwara is where seva is learned: strangers' shoes, the Guru's presence, haumai scrubbed.
Bebe's generation is just more used to the gurdwara, so it feels right to her.
the food bank isn't really seva, because it isn't run by a gurdwara.
games.why: Bebe's best case isn't habit: it's that seva in the Guru's house trains the self, and the sangat runs on those hands. Harjit's best case is Ang 26.

practice: Take a pen and a scrap of paper. Write one line by hand: the one seva you could keep, and the day it happens. Then hold the paper for the sit and read your own handwriting slowly, once at the start and once at the end.

wordCard.voice: Seva. Selfless service, done for others with no wage, in the gurdwara and in the world.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: seva, service given freely; in Gurbani often paired with the Guru, gur ki seva.

carryVoice: For the road: my seva, small enough to keep and real enough to count. Day 1711, chosen.

sources.ref: Ang 26, Sri Raag, Guru Nanak (vich dunia sev kamaaeeai, taa dargah baisan paaeeai), paraphrased
